sections.label: Head
sections.text:
Violent vertigo on going upstairs. Eyes
sunken ; broad, blue circles around. Violent sneezing.
Nose cold. Must be wrapped up with warm cloths.

sections.label: Mouth
sections.text:
Tongue enlarged; deep, irregular ulcer;
modular swelling. Mouth hot and dry; little thirst.

sections.label: fever
sections.text:
Copious green vomiting, commencing in evening of 1st day and
lasting all night ; every hour between the time a soporous
state ; on the 2d day greenish vomiting every two hours,
lessening the 3d and 4th day. — Br.

Vomits large masses. — Br.

Before midnight twice vomiting, with bellyache and the great-
est anxiety. — R.Sch.

Vomiting with the pain in the loins. — Br.
^^ Scrobiculum and Stomach. Irritability of stomach, vomit-
ing liquid, first bilious and afterwards coffee-colored, "with a
burning pain. — Robertson.

With pressure in stomach : very little appetite ; bitter taste ;
belching ; nausea and obstinate constipation. — Eisenmenger.

ARSENICUM HYDROGENISATUM. 104

With the dead feeling in the limbs five hours after inhalation,
violent cutting pain in region of stomach and below it, it
compels him to moan constantly. — R.Sch.

A weary feeling in stomach, with pressure in temples. —

Stomach empty, two inflamed spots in the large curvature,
where the mucous membrane could very easily be peeled off.
Post mortem. — Br.

Pain in epigastrium and vomiting of food, —

Very sensitive epigastrium and tormenting hiccough ; 2d day.
—Br.

Pressure in epigastric region during chill. — Eisenmenger,

Pressure of hand causes dull pain in epigastrium. — O'Reilly.

Pains in epigastrium. — Ollivier.
^^ Hypochondria. Liver painful to pressure ; after three or four
hours — Ollivier.

Liver was congested, without alteration of the cells. — Ollivier.

Liver deep indigo blue, not enlarged, gall bladder full to burst-
ing.— Br.

Softening of the spleen. — Ollivier.
^^ Abdomen, Loins and Groins. A slight pressure in abdomen ;
5th day. — R.Sch.

Pressing pain below the diaphragm, on the left side of abdo-
men ; 1st day. — C.Hg.

Violent cutting in region of navel, at intervals. — R.Sch.

Colic with vomiting, before midnight.

Pains in various parts of abdomen, worse left side, followed by
great weakness, most in lower limbs; 1st day. — C.Hg.

Sensation of weakness in abdomen and pinching stitches.

An undecided, but exceedingly unpleasant sensation, as from a
stone lying in abdomen, as if all had changed into a stone ;
he begged for a laxative, but neither injections nor repeated
stools (after Magn. sulph.) made any change, belching did not
relieve. — Sch.

Glowing heat in abdomen, with cold limbs. — Sch.

Burning pain through the whole alimentary canal. — Robertson.

I Abdomen burning, outside; cold feet. ^Yellow fever.

A gurgling noise in left side of abdomen from incarcerated
flatus, causing colicky pain, threatening to become severe ;
he has to lie on the belly, or bent together, and wants to be
well covered; very sensitive to the cold; morning, 3 a.m.;
2d day. —C.Hg.

Distension of abdomen during chills. — Eisenmenger.

Gaseous distension of abdomen. Post mortem. — ^Br.

Integuments of abdomen look greenish, most on the sides. — Br.

Violent itching below the last rib on the extreme left ; 3d day.
-C.Hg
^^ Rectum and Stool. Weak sensation, as if relaxed, and as if

105 ARSENICUM HYDROGENISATUM.

diarrhoea followed, the whole would fall out; evening, 1st

day. — C.Hg.
Urging as to diarrhoea ; noon, 2d day. — C.Hg.
Less wind passed after urination in the morning ; 2d day. — C.

Hg.
Copious passage of wind and looseness ; after Magn. sulpli. did

not relieve. — Sch.
Several openings the 4th day. — Sch.
Soft stool at 4 P.M.; 2d day. — C.Hg.
Frequent bilious stools. — Br.

The usual morning stool is omitted and appears in the after-
noon ; the same 6th, 7th and 8th day. — F.K.
Two copious, offensive stools, 5 p.m., followed by a painless

evacuation of half a pound of red urine, containing real

blood corpuscles ; 1st day.' — Ollivier.
The first morning stool on the 10th day, full of holes like

lava.— F.K.
*Obstinate constipation. — Eisenmenger.

■ Constipation, with a feeling of heaviness and stiffness, like a

weight in abdomen. — F.W.Payne.

Constipation, with fever. — Robertson.

Stool, with vertigo, weakness and crawling. — Br.

Thumping, knocking pains in region of perineum, near the anus;
forenoon, 2d day. — C.Hg.

Frequent flying pains in perineum, to the anus, or, upwards in
the anterior wall of rectum ; 1st week. — C.Hg.
^^ Urinary Organs. Unpleasant sensation of pressure in region
of kidneys, rapidly increasing, extending over the back to
between the shoulders, not violent until night ; it continued
without interruption, and increasing, with urging to urinate ;
the urine is dark-red, and a thick coagulum of pure blood
is formed ; next day the color the same, but no coagulum,
pain in kidneys equally violent ; the 3d day the pain less
violent ; color more bright, still bloody ; the same the 4th
day ; on the 6th day without bloody color. — R.Sch.

■ Pressure in the kidneys, extending to shoulder-blades, with

pain in region of kidneys during desire to urinate, d Yellow

sections.label: fever
sections.text:
Kidneys enlarged, with very marked injection, most in the tu-
bular substance ; the cells of both substances granulated. —
Ollivier.

Kidneys deep indigo -blue through the whole substance, the
left enlarged similar to the spleen, the right smaller. — Br.

Scanty, foaming urine in the morning, depositing a sediment ;
2d day.— C.Hg.

* Called " obstinate" by the Old School, which is transferring a quality of
their own mind to the colon.

ARSENICUM HYDROGENISATUM. 106

From 1st to 8th day less urine ; on the 9th more, but brown,

with a suspended cloud. — F.K.
No urination 2d day. — Ollivier.
The urine is suppressed ; from 4 p.m. no urine till the next

morning; 1st day. — C.Hg.
No urine 1st night ; very little next night ; 3d to 6th day. — Br.
Very small quantities of urine, deposits some blood ; 6th day.
Bladder empty, no change. — Br.
Urine very dark, orange-colored ; 5th day. — F.K.
Inky urine ; on boiling and adding Nitric acid a reddish-brown

coagulum resembling that which we obtain from boiling blood,

is deposited. — J.Vogel.
Urine not so frequent, but more profuse evening ; 6th day. — F.K.
During the night no urine ;, in the morning dark, reddish-brown,

with red gelatinous and bluish-red sediment ; 8th day. — F.K.
Afternoon, dark urine, with a rose-colored deposit on the walls

of the chamber ; 9th day. — F.K.
Urine like porter, with a cloudy deposit; 10th day. — F.K.
Urine darker on the 13th day. — F.K.
Urine red, scanty ; 3d day.
Urine dark, reddish-black ; formed a thick clot of blood in the

vessel. — Sch.
Soon a painless discharge of two ounces of blood through the

urethra; repeated with the shuddering. — Br.
Hsematuria ; passed two ounces of blood through urethra. —

O'Reilly.
Four tablespoonfulls of blood from the urethra ; 2d day. — Br.
Four pints of bloody urine, containing arsenic. — Robertson.
Discharge of inky urine. — Bennecke.

I Urine dark, blackish-red, with pure blood. ^ Yellow fever.
■ Discharge at times of large quantities of pale urine. — F.W.

Payne.
^^ Male Sexual Organs. Sexual irritation on the glans penis,

almost irresistible with the morning erection ; 2d day ; it

continues after rising and passing water ; all first week. —

Deep in pelvis when crouching down, an unbearable sensation
of numbness, with a waving as if it would break, then a hor-
rible feeling, but of short duration; ibrenoon, 11th day. — C.

A pain in symphysis pubis, no redness there, but it is exceed-
ingly sensitive to the touch, also when coughing or bending
forward; 16th day. — F.K.

Violent pricking pain on a small spot over the right groin, of-
ten repeated, like a throbbing; 1st day. — C.Hg.

Unbearable pain in both groins, exactly where the spermatic
cords emerge, as if everything would fall or slip out there ;
exceedingly sensitive in standing ; > when sitting ; still

107 ARSENICUM HYDROGEOTSATUM.

more when pressing on it with both hands ; afternoon, 10th
day ; the same feeling returns on the 12th day at 2 p.m. —
C.Hg.

Pain in the left side of penis; 1st day. — C.Hg.

In the 3d week the whole foreskin and glans is covered with
little blisters containing pus ; they burst and form very small
round flat ulcers ; alone on the outer surface of the foreskin
he counted sixty-five, they healed after ten to twelve days. —
R.Sch.*
^' Voice and Larynx. Squeaking voice ; immediately after in-
halation.— Br.

Whispering voice. — O'Reilly.

The voice remains whispering and gets very weak in the even-
ing.— Br.

Voice has lost its timbre, sounds as if broken, but not hoarse ;
5th day.— F.K.

Pain near the larynx when speaking, right side; 8th day. — F.K.

A drawing sensation from head toward larynx, right side.

With a slight hemming or hawking he raises with great ease a
soft, round and smooth lump of phlegm the size of a filbert,
when awaking at 3 A.M.; 2d day. — C-Hg.

I His customary hawking up of phlegm ceases ; 6th day. — F.K.
^^ Respiration. Ammoniacal odor of the breath ; 5th to 7th day.
— Br.

Rapid breathing.

Constriction of chest : with the nausea ; with the chill.

Want of breath ; gasping for air.

Breathing relieved after Sinapism and Amm. aeet.; after three
or four hours. — Ollivier.

Oppression of chest during chill. — Eisenmenger;
" Cough. In the forenoon frequent coughing, with a pain in the
perineum ; 3d day. — F.K.

When he coughs in the evening headache in upper and back
part of head; 6th day. — F.K.

A little cough very often, without inner irritation, as from a
pressure over the chest ; after eating ice cream, at first better
(also the whole chest), but afterwards worse ; 6th day. — F.K.

Cough increases from 9 to 10 a.m., most while conversing in
the room ; 7th day. — F.K.

In the evening the cough comes now from the depths of the
chest, is looser; sputa relieved; 7th day. — F.K.

Cough comes from the front upper part of chest ; 9th day. — F.K.

Sweats when coughing; 11th day. — F.K.

A sensation as if the whole thorax was laced tightly, with rapid
breathing, without cough or rattling of phlegm ; after three
hours. — Ollivier.

* Was the j'oung man syphilitic ? Ars. met. brings out dormant syphilis.
—C.Hg.

ARSENICUM HYDROGENISATUM. 108

^^ Inner Chest and Lungs. Pressure in region above the breast-
bone, all across, on the 4th day ; worse on 5th. — F.K.

A painful pressure in upper part of chest, where it commences
to become sore to pressure, disappears when perspiring;
7th day.— F.K.

Pressure over whole chest, with great anxiety ; 7 th day ; the
pressure is lessened by gaping ; 9th day. — F.K.

Pain in chest is gone in the morning, returns towards 11 A.M.;
11th day.— F.K.

Pressure over the chest produces a slight cough. —

Pain across chest, like a beating deep in right side, near the
middle, drawing towards the left. — R.H.

A glowing sensation in chest after the chilly feeling. —

Back part of lungs are congested; 2d day. — Ollivier.

Lungs collapsed, containing very little air, otherwise normal.
—Br.

In the cavities of the pleura two pints of reddish-brown, odor-
less fluid. — Br.

^^ Heart, Pulse and Circulation. A cutting pain near the last

left ribs.
A knocking, thumping pain in heart, deep in chest, extends

towards the right side ; forenoon, 2d day. — C.Hg.
Palpitation ; 7th day. — Br.
Heart pale, relaxed, empty of blood ; only a little fluid in the

pericardium . — Br.
Pulse small and rapid. — Eisenmenger.
Pulse 90, weak.— O'Reilly.

Fever with a full, hard, frequent pulse. — Robertson.
Pulse strong and frequent. —
Pulse 107 ; 2d day.—
I Pulse frequent. ^Yellow fever.
Pulse 90 in the morning, 128 at 10 o'clock, very small and

soft; 7th day.— F.K.
After meals the pulse is more full and more frequent ; 7th day.

—F.K.
Pulse intermits when awaking in the night, with anxiety and

thoughts of death ; 7th day. — F.K.
Pulse 60 in the morning, and irregular ; in the forenoon 52 ;

8th day.— F.K.
In the evening pulse 56, the same after eating ; later 60, and

tensive, as if turned or twisted ; some beats retarded for

more than a second, followed by a few quicker beats ; 8th

day.— F.K.
Pulse 64, every other beat stronger, like the pendulum of a

clock placed obliquely ; 8th day. — F.K.
Pulse 64, limping in the morning of 9th day ; at noon, 112,

limping till 1 P.M., and softer; 3 p.m., limping again and

intermitting; changing from quicker to slower. — F.K.

109 ARSENICUM HYDROGENISATUM.

Pulse 76 in the morning; at 11 a.m., 84 to 88; 11th day. —
F.K.

Pulse more frequent after the meal at noon ; 14th day. — F.K.

Pulse very frequent and small with the chill. —

Pulse 110 after Siniapism and Ammon. acet. — Ollivier.

Pulse 90, but weak, after four hours ; small, 92, lessened
temperature of skin next day ; 80, strong, with sensitive
epigastrium, 2d day ; 76, and painless epigastrium ; later,
same day ; 76, Sd day ; 80, 5th day ; same, 6th day ; 102
in the morning, 7th day ; 76 at noon ; later, 80 ; death next
morning. — Br.

The breathing very frequent, and the pulse imperceptible be-
fore death. —

Pulse imperceptible after increased respiration ; becoming un-
conscious ; evening 5th day, death. — Ollivier.

Complete cessation of pulse. — R.Sch.

I Pulse quite imperceptible, d Collapse in cholera.
^^ Outer Chest. Rheumatic pains over the breast-bone lessen
when perspiring ; 2d day. — F.K.

Pain in middle of sternum ; < when he walks about ; 10th day.
—F.K.

Pain in chest, in the bones and intercostal muscles ; at the same
time pain in arm.

Want of breath, and gasping for air. — Ea.

In left side of chest, near the nipple, as if raw and sore, with
the pressive pain ; 4th day. — F.K.

The pain in chest is concentrated in the left side, above the
nipple; 9th day. — F.K.

A pressure over the chest, a few inches below the upper end of
breast-bone, with a pressure on the breast-bone ; 6th day. —
F.K.

Sore, raw feeling over the whole chest; 8th day. — F.K.

Chest hurts when coughing, breathing, and when pressed ; 8th
day.— F.K.

A crawling, as if warm drops were running over the chest,
stopped by pressing with the finger; 11th day. — F.K.
^^ Neck and Back, Tearing pain in neck during chill. — Eisen-
menger.

Feverish in the neck, forenoon ; 13th day. — F.K.

Stiffness in the neck and between the shoulders, begins in the
morning ; > when going out or moving about ; 7th and 8th
day. — C.Hg.

aPain as if something was sticking below the right shoulder-
blade ; increased at first, and disappeared after three hours

sections.label: sleep
sections.text:
C.Hg.

Backache like on the first days, returned towards evening on
the 7th day, not so violent, but much harder to bear; in-
creased next evening and in the night, causing loud lamenta-

ARSENICUM HYDROGENISATUM. 110

tions ; sitting relieves it a little, but he is too weak to sit
long ; relieved towards evening of 9tli day by application
of cloths dipped in warm milk. — R.Sch.

Crawlino; over the shoulders and back. —

A glow in the back after chilliness. —

Shuddering over single parts of back. —

Pain in region of kidneys became exceedingly severe, with urg-
ing to urinate. — Sch.

An unpleasant pressive feeling in region of kidney, which
rapidly increased and spread up the back to between shoul-
ders ; after four hours. — Sch.

Pressure between the shoulders. — R.Sch.

Very violent pain in lumbar region. — Ollivier. '

Slight pain in lumbar region. — O'Reilly.

Some pains in the loins when the "falling asleep" of the limbs
passed away. — Br.

Pain in loins with vomiting. — Br.

Behind and above the right hip, on a small spot near the spine,
a very great pain ; increased in walking ; has to sit down. —
C.Hg.

Backache in small of back, as after having taken cold ; even-
ing, 2d day.— F.K.

Violent pains in sacrum, after three hours.

A dull pain on upper part of sacrum, on a place the size of a
hand, interferes for one or two minutes with his breathing ;
it swells and feels as if something was filled up ; with in-
creased pain ; 8th day. — F.K.
^^ Upper Limbs. Sore aching spot on the right acromion ; 8th
day.— F.K

Pain from the tip of shoulder down towards the point of elbow ;
9th day.— F.K.

Painful twitching in the shoulders.

A warm, almost burning cut, like with a small knife, in right
upper arm, from near the shoulder down towards the elbow ;
soon after inhalation. — F.K.

Flying stitches in the arms. — R.Sch.

Tearing pain and stitches in upper limbs, during chill. — Eisen-
menger.

In the elbows and upper arms the same pain as in the knee. —
R.Sch.

Earning pain in both elbows, more in the right ; 9th day. — F.K.

Pains in elbows and upper arms ; in five hours. — Sch.

Feeling of deadness of hands extending to middle of forearms.
—R.Sch.

Arms and hands very tired, as if burning.

Flying pains in right hand and fingers ; 2d day. — C.Hg.

Swollen veins on the hands; 7th day. — F.K.

Ill ARSENICUM HYDROGENISATUM.

Middle finger, left and inner side, and second joint red and
swollen ; the 14tli day ; gone the 15th day. — F.K.

Itching on the first joint of the left middle finger, inner side,
on a small spot, where a very small blister is ; after the 1st
week. — CHg.
^^ Lower Limbs. Slight thumping pain on a small spot behind
the right hip-bone. — CHg.

Pimple on the nates, impedes walking; 15th day. — F.K.

Quivering in left thigh, inner side, towards the front, in a short
line, evening, till night ; 9th day ; again on the 10th day,
in the afternoon. — F.K.

Pain on inner side of both thighs, most right side, whence it
extends to near the anus ; 12th day. — F.K.

Pain on inner side of both thighs, mostly towards the os pelvis :
15th day.— F.K.

Violent itching on left thigh, on the inner side, a few inches
above the knee ; 7th day. — CHg.

After getting up, when placing his legs higher than the body, a
violent pain above the left knee ; soreness in the muscles or
tendons, under the skin ; gets better when moving about ;
evening, 1st day ; the next day it still pains, but more be-
low the knee, with a lame feeling when kneeling ; his limbs
break down when going up stairs; noon, 2d day. — CHg.

Above the right patella a pain on pressure, also in the bend of
the knee ; increases after lying still a good while ; evening.
16th day.— F.K. ^

On getting up and beginning to move, after lying especially
in a somewhat fatiguing position, a pain in left I: nee, as if it
was inwardly crushed, but not in the bones ; it increases to
a kind of burning, and only disappears after continuing to
move ; 8th to 10th day. — C.Hg.

Rheumatic, gouty, tearing pain in knee-joints. — R.Sch.

Pains in the knees during the chill. — R.Sch.

Pain in hollow of left knee, when rising from a seat, and in the
beginning of walking ; 3d day. — F.K.

Sensation in bend of left knee as if beaten ; a cold and burn-
ing pain ; < on beginning to move, especially after lying ;
the whole 1st week. — CHg.

In the bones of the leg below the right knee, a throbbing pain,
drawing downwards. —

Pains in lower limbs, especially right side, lasting two hours.
— Br.

Flying stitches in lower limbs. — R.Sch.

Pain in lower limbs, more in the right. — O'Reilly.

Flying, cutting pains in left leg, from the shin to the ankle ;
at same time on the last left ribs; 2d day — CHg.

Pain in left leg, after sitting ; < going down stairs, with break-
ing down of the knees ; 2d day. — CHg.

ARSENICUM HYDROGENISATUM. 112

Lower limbs become rigid later than the arms. — Br.

Feet get numb, as if dead, up to the knees. — R.Sch.

Weakness, most in the lower limbs. — Z.

Left foot hurts again when ri^'ing, most towards the external
margin ; 12th day. — F.K.

Feet, usually colder than the rest of the body, are now warmer ;
3d day.— F.K.

Sweat all over, but not on the right foot. — F.K.

Pain in right heel. —

Flying pains in the feet. —

Pain in left foot-joint when walking ; 3d day. — F.K.

The left foot-joint he cannot move, even when lying in bed;
«th day.— F.K.

Can not move the foot, and is unable to get up ; 9th day. — F.K.

Great pain in left foot, from one ankle-bone to the other, pass-
ing across above the joint, worst on a small spot of the dor-
sum of the foot ; a red-yellow streak on the top of the foot,
near the toes ; from the fourth to the second toe ; the pain
is awful, turns him pale ; most painful in the moving of the
foot-joint ; 1st day. — F.K.

A red streak on the ankle-joint, where the pain was day be-
fore ; 11th day.— F.K.

In left foot, most on the sole, pains prevent stepping on it ;
worse in motion, less in bed; pains in the middle, as if con-
tracted lengthways ; when stepping on it a painful stretch ;
3d day ; much worse the 4th. — F.K.

Pain in left sole prevents walking in the forenoon ; less in the
afternoon ; << in the evening, especially after rising from a
seat; all the pains in sole, heel, and the whole foot, extend
upwards; 6th day. — F.K.

Pains in left sole, foot and knee, increase in the evening ; 6th
day. — F.K.

Pain from the sole towards the middle toe ; very much worse
when the first toe-joints are bent ; 8th day. — F.K.

Tickling in hollow of left foot; 10th day. — F.K.

Pain on pressure of balls of toes, sore and thrilling, most ball
of middle toe ; the pain extends along all the toes ; 8th day.
—F.K.

With every attempt to step on the feet all the toes hurt, as if
in the tendons, up to the foot-joint ; 8th day. — F.K.

The once chilblained ball of the right big toe gets more pain-
ful ; 16th day.— F.K.

Thumping pain in right big toe increasing in warmth. — C.Hg.

The left middle toe is exceedingly painful when touched, most
underneath, on the ball and in the first joint, and from there
to the big toe and inside the ankle ; 8th day. — F.K.

Sensation as if a splinter lodged under the nail of the left mid-
dle toe; 9th to 10th day.— F.K.

113 ARSENICUM HYDROGENISATUM.

^* Limbs in General. Soon after inhalation pain in lower limbs,
most right side, with a numbness, jfirst in upper limbs, then
in the lower, followed by a crawling sensation, for two hours.
—Br.

Very sensitive, gouty, tearing pains iu upper arms, elbows and
knee-joints. — Br.

Throbbing pains in bones of left upper arm, extending down-
wards, three and five times every hour; the same in the bones
of the right lower limb below the knee ; also extending down-
wards.— Br. C.Hg.

Stitches in arms and feet. — R.Sch.

Weakness in limbs. — Bennecke.

Arms get cold and stiff first, then lower limbs. — Br.

Coldness of limbs. — R.Sch. Ollivier.

I Coldness of limbs. — F.W.Payne.

Unpleasant crawling in hands and feet, and flying stitches in
upper and lower limbs ; 7th day. — R.Sch.
^^ Rest. Position. Motion. Tired in hands and arms, after
moderate exertion (carrying a child), they burn from weak-
ness; 1st day. — C.Hg.

Very little inclined to do any work. — Eisenmenger.

Difficult walking. —

Walking up stairs, vertigo. —

Motion difficult. — Ollivier.

While walking, chilly. —

All pains increase during motion ; in rest they also first in-
crease, but get better afterwards. — F.K.

Weak even when sitting. — C.Hg.

Such a yeakness that he cannot sit ; on the 3d day able to do
a few steps ; still very weak 7th day ; somewhat better 10th
day and following.^ — R.Sch.

Getting up he feels so weak and chilly that he is obliged to lie
down again ; evening, 8th day. — F.K.

Such a sensation of weakness with the headache and vertigo,
that he has to lie down ; 3d day. —

Colic better lying on belly, or better frofli bending together. —
^® Nerves. Restlessness and anxiety. — Robertson.

The greatest bodily restlessness ; 5th day. — Br.

Prostration with anxiety; vertigo, nausea, and troublesome
costiveness. — Berzelius.

Suddenly after the inhalation he feels himself poisoned ; an in-
describable exhaustion and nausea overwhelms him ; hardly
